utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Stamp, the Chamber highly appreciates that you give us some extra time in the morning to read the correspondence of the last day, but the Chamber -- I know that this clock is not the only one in this building. But when all the clocks were certainly past 9.00, we -- you still gave us the opportunity to read letters instead of starting with the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you asked to address the Chamber for three minutes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. The reason for which the Defence has decided to address you is because Defence doesn't really know what is coming from the accusation, from the Prosecution. We no longer know whether the Prosecution -- we don't know where they are going any more. We don't know anything about this. All we know is that ties have been cut and we really don't see whether the Prosecution is going to continue in this manner. In other terms, Mr. President, yesterday we had a serious problem. We lost a lot of time because the Prosecution told us, with regard to two incidents, incident number 11 and incident number 2, I think, that the Defence didn't do what it was obliged to do. It didn't inform the Prosecution that we were going to question the witness with regard to these specific events. Since yesterday, Mr. Stamp has told me that he doesn't think this information hasn't been provided to him, but I'm told that this isn't the case. I don't have the documents in front of me because I was basing myself on the principle that this matter had been dealt with. It seems the Prosecution refuses to take into consideration elements that have been communicated to them very clearly in detail and we do not appreciate the fact that something was staged last night. It was something pulled out of a hat. It was a trick. And we don't appreciate the fact that we can claim quite coolly that certain elements weren't provided whereas they were. There was a mistake, a small mistake made by the Defence. Since we didn't officially inform about incident 11, but elements 11 and 12 [as interpreted] were proceed these -- these two elements proceed from the same point, from the same firing point. And, Mr. President, we cannot accept that we should waste precious time in order to deal with problems that are not real problems. It is not possible for us to continue in this manner and we would appreciate if this Trial Chamber could sanction such an attitude on the part of the Prosecution. Thank you. For the sake of the transcript, naturally, the points concerned are 11 and 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you have a specific sanction in mind already or would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, not at all, but I quite simply don't think that it would be useful. When I say "sanctions" I am not asking for anything. But I don't think that this should happen again and I don't think it is useful for the Prosecution to affirm that we haven't done our work whereas this is not true. So unfortunately this is not the Defence's problem. I think that the Defence has access to all the three languages that are spoken here and perhaps even two others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... consider the matter. Apart from that, is the Defence ready to continue the examination of the witness? Yes, then Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony yesterday. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we will very briefly go back to the testimony that you were giving, but, first of all, I apologise. Good day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are going to move back to your previous testimony and I am specifically interested in the question of stray bullets, on the issue of stray bullets. You spoke about stray bullets with regard to the wall of the cemetery which was made of concrete. In the zone that we are interested in, the one you were positioned in, were there any other elements that could have similarly caused what we call ricochets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific and tell us what you are referring to, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the monuments in the Jewish cemetery, concrete houses, high buildings, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The buildings that you are referring to, were they numerous, were there not that many of them? Could you tell us what the concentration of such objects was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On our side, the lines of the cemetery, of the Jewish cemetery, there were houses with about five to ten metres between them. And this was the case on their side, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, was there fighting that was quite intense on several occasions, was there serious fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, to the best of your knowledge, on the basis of your experience, where did the bullets that ricochetted, where did they go, or rather where could they go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In various directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "in various directions" is it possible that these bullets could also go off into -- into the town and stray into an urban area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if they were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you know if certain weapons such as, for example, weapons from which bursts of fire can be fired, do you know whether one of their characteristics is to have a trajectory which makes it somehow drift away the more the object is distant from the point of departure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All anti-tank and ordinary machine-guns and automatic rifles are of this kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you tell us, could you remind us what the official range of a light machine-gun is -- I will withdraw that question. I will withdraw that question. I apologise. Did you have personal knowledge of military persons or civilians who were wounded as a result of ricochets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but on our side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. How can you be certain that this was the result of a ricochet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the wounds were on the whole, slight, and not very deep. Direct hits would usually go through the body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, do you know whether your unit had relations with representatives of the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether these people, these representatives ever protested with someone from your unit for any reason whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in our unit, but it was suggested to us that they would come to visit us, the French Battalion from UNPROFOR would come, which was on the other side by the Muslims, and the Russian Battalion which arrived later, which was on our side of the Jewish cemetery. They know this very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But as far as you know, these people, regardless of their nationality and I am referring to the UN personnel, did they ever launch a protest with you of any kind with regard to the laws of war? And I mean this in the widest possible sense.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't lodge a protest with us, but very often they would relay to Muslim units --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. I am not talking about the other side. I am only talking about protests that may have been lodged with you. Thank you very much, Witness. And this is my last question, this is purely hypothetical, please take this into account the fact that it's just a hypothesis, if one of your comrades in arms committed an act that at the time might be considered to be a serious violation or even a crime, what would have happened, how would the army, how would the unit have reacted to such an act? What sort of sanctions would have been implemented? What do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if that had happened, a report would have been given to the commander, and then it would have been followed up. But this didn't happen. This is all I know. It never happened during the four years of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you personally informed of the fact that if you violated -- and this is still a hypothesis -- if your military obligations were violated, would you be suggested to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would you please not lead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, with regard to this issue concerning sanctions, was information provided to the lines, were the men provided with such information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, through the commanders of detachments, platoons and companies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Your evidence, if I have understood you correctly, is that the military hierarchy provided you with all these instructions and all the men -- right up to the men, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine the witness, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Cross-examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were involved in the 3rd Battalion from the early part of 1992 until 1995 when it was disbanded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it your evidence that during that time you did not know or hear of any of the members of your battalion being prosecuted for any offences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know of any such cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to you, you fought with all five companies of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We went to provide assistance when the fighting was intense and when quite a few people were wounded in the 2nd, 3rd and 5th Company, we had to go and assist them. So the rest of us were cut off because we were the prominent position as the 3rd Company. We were in a more prominent position than the 5th and 4th companies, not to mention the 1st and 2nd companies. I can provide you with examples.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask about that later. Thank you very much. Now, you spoke a lot yesterday about sniping at positions held by your battalion. Did your battalion have snipers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one. Each company has to have a sniper as per establishment. An ordinary man, though, he is not a sportsman or a real shooter. Unfortunately, he is not alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you are concerned in your battalion there was only five snipers at any one time, one for each company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not at any given moment. Later on when the units were established, at the beginning there was nothing. We didn't have any weapons. We had hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A simple answer to the question, a yes or no would do. Did your brigade have a sniping platoon in the Grbavica area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your brigade employ snipers in the high buildings on the -- in the part of Grbavica that it controlled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen a sniper's rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, captured from the Muslims -- a Pam rifle, an anti-aircraft gun, an M-7, it is the latest sniper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are saying that the only weapon that you describe as a sniper's weapon that you saw during the conflict was one that was captured from the opposing side; is that what you are saying, that this was the only weapon that you would describe as a sniper's weapon that you saw during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I saw ordinary sniping --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I think that, according to the Rules, we shouldn't interrupt the witness too frequently, but I want to underline this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will try not to interrupt the witness, but may I ask if I could -- perhaps if I do it might appear impolite, if the witness could be directed, and I'm not saying he's being evasive or anything, but sometimes he responds outside of the questions I ask which takes up time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you to, Witness, to carefully listen to the question and specifically answer to that question. So if, for example, the question is whether you have ever seen a sniper rifle, then please answer yes or no. You added where the rifle came from that you had seen, and only in following questions you testified that you did not only see sniper rifles captured from the Muslim side, but also other sniper rifles. So if any further information is needed, counsel will certainly ask you for it, but please first concentrate on the question and answer that question to start with. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you speak of ordinary sniping weapons, what is a name of the weapon that you would consider to be an ordinary sniping weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A hunting sniper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if you know, is the name of the weapon that you would consider to be an ordinary sniper's rifle?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the killing range of that weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This depends on how good the bullets are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you explain that? What do you mean this depends on how good the bullets are? I asked you if you know the killing range of the sniper's weapon that you referred to, and you said it depends on how good the bullets are. Could you explain that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because if ammunition is old, then it doesn't have such a range, and it also depends on the terrain. But the range, 200, perhaps. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Depends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if the ammunition is good, what is the killing range of a sniper's weapon, as far as your experience in the war is concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 800 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of positions did the sniper in your company locate himself at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the line. Facing the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of a commander in your brigade by the name of Zeljko Kozomara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't know him by that -- the name and the surname, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there were screens or curtains, I think, which to some degree --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of the UNPROFOR forces putting up antisniping barricades on the ABiH side of Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of the UNPROFOR operating antisniping units on the ABiH side of Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I may have heard something about it, but I don't know. I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of an antisniping agreement that came into effect in the early part of 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that there was a truce, and that during the truce over 100 civilians and soldiers died from snipers during this truce. But there was an order, I don't know what the date was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer is not really responding to the question. I am talking about the early part of 1994, and I will repeat the question: Do you know of an antisniping agreement in the early part of 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you on the lines in the vicinity of the Jewish cemetery in the early part of 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just by the cemetery there was always the line there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of units from outside of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps being brought in to crush VRS sniping units, VRS units that were sniping at civilians from the area of the Jewish cemetery in the early part of 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not where we were, in our company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, and I note your answer, "not where you were" but I will rephrase the question and I would like you to answer it: Are you aware of units, military units from outside of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps being brought to the area of the Jewish cemetery to suppress sniping units that had been shooting at civilians? And that is in the early part of 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that the witness has answered the previous question very clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, let me just guide you. If you would like to make this objection, you could say, which is a usual expression, "question asked; question answered." That would do. Then in legal terms, it is clear to everyone what you intend to say. The question has not been answered. Please -- let me. You have heard the question of Mr. Stamp, whether any units were brought in in early 1994 from outside the Sarajevo Romanija Corps in order to suppress sniper activity in the area of the Jewish cemetery. Could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I answered. I answered, no, not in my company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now the question is, which was not in your company, might have been in other units. The question is not limited to your company, but the question is whether you knew anything about such a thing, even if it was not in your unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't have any personal knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What do you mean by "personal knowledge"? Did you hear from someone about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On a map yesterday you pointed to several buildings and you said fire emanated from those buildings every day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I am going to ask you if you are sure about this "every day" aspect. Is it an exaggeration or is it true, that to your certain knowledge, fire emanated from those buildings every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992, 1993, almost every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you now say it was not every day, but almost every day; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me clarify --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, please. Time is limited. Thank you very much for the offer. I just want to know if it is now your evidence that though there might not have been fire every single day, it was most days in 1992 and 1993; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally see and witness fire coming from the Holiday Inn most days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly, most days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it, therefore, that your evidence is that in 1992, 1993, and 1994, on most days you saw fire coming from the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I see, page 14, line 3, we are talking about 1992, 1993. On the same page, line 9, we are talking about 1992, and 1993, and we suddenly moved to 1992, 1993, and 1994. That confuses me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr. President. I really wanted to stick to what he had said, 1992 and 1993, earlier. However, he did answer nonetheless. Could the witness be shown Exhibit 3 -- the first photograph was what? 341.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that this photograph was taken from the left side of the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that everyone understands by "the left side" it being the western side -- I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our side. From our side, from our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to your positions were throughout on the western side of the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I am not asking about the photograph right now. Just listen to what I am asking. According to you, throughout the entire period of conflict, your lines were always to the west side of the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the west side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is a photograph of part of the vicinity taken from the vicinity of your lines, if I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point out to us which part of the Holiday Inn that you saw fire emanating from almost every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The central part of the Holiday Inn, it had two holes with a radius of about 1 metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object. This is not the testimony of the witness. The witness never said that he saw Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. firing -- let me finish. Let me finish my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we should ask the witness to take his headphones off or to leave the courtroom, if you start commenting on what the testimony of the witness was. So I will not let you continue until --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well, let's do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But first, may I ask the witness -- I think we never asked him whether he speaks -- could you -- do you understand any English or French?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then please take your headphones off again. And Mr. Usher, I would like as a rule, if the witness stays, I would like him not to have the transcript on his screen, but I take it that it is a picture now. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President what I wanted to say is that on page 14, line 16 and then 17, the testimony of this witness was not that he had seen fire coming from the Holiday Inn on a daily basis. He didn't say every day. And this is not what the transcript says. He is talking about many days of firing, but certainly not the expression used by Mr. Stamp, which was "every day."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If -- yes, please respond. As far as I can see it now, we have heard the objection. Please respond and then...

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Having marked these positions yesterday on the map, including the Holiday Inn being number "3", he was asked by counsel: "Q. Mr. D11, during the course of 1992 and 1994, can you tell us whether and how often soldiers fired from the positions that you have marked with the weapons that you had mentioned." He had earlier said sniping from time to time Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Stamp slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question continued: "How often did this occur?" And his answer was: "Well, this occurred on a daily basis, several times a day." Then today I asked if it was an exaggeration about daily -- I didn't ask him about several times a day. And he said, well, not really daily, but most days. And today I was asking him specifically about the Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us the lines of yesterday

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to -- what I find in yesterday's transcript is a question saying. "Q. Mr. D11, in the course of 1992 and 1994, can you tell us whether and how often soldiers fired from the positions that you have marked and with the weapons you have mentioned." And then the answer was: "Well this occurred on a daily basis." That means, and that is how I understand the testimony to be today as well, is that the witness testified that from those positions there was on a daily basis or at least at an almost daily basis, fire, but that would not necessarily mean that from the Holiday Inn it would also be on a daily or an almost daily basis. If you would agree with that, could you then please rephrase the question. On the other hand, the question was specifically about from where from the Holiday Inn. So whether this was on a daily basis, it should not be misrepresented, but it could create no confusion in respect of the question itself, that is, from what part of the Holiday Inn. Witness, could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I, before we proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: To narrow yesterday's testimony to the Holiday Inn, I did ask him at line 14, at page 14, line 12, "did you personally see and witness fire coming from the Holiday Inn --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And yes, he said he practically saw it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I overlooked that. I must say that on page 14, line 12, it -- the testimony was that it was mostly most days that the witness personally saw fire coming from the Holiday Inn. Mr. Stamp, I have to apologise. I misinterpreted. No I -- but the matter has been settled. I think it was Mr. Piletta-Zanin, unless you would disagree, I would see on page 14, line 14, this is what the witness testified, that most days he saw fire coming from the Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. The question was please point out and explain to us where it was on that Holiday Inn building that you saw fire coming from most days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the floors, from the high floors, there would be fire that we could see. There was a light from the fire and there were shots that were being fired at us. That was, they were firing at our back because this building is behind us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you say "from the top, from floor near the top" how many times floors from the top of the building did you see this firing coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As much as you can see here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe you didn't understand the question. You said from the "from the floors towards the top." How many floors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five, six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So firing came from five to six floors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't count them, but they were changing places. Understand, they were changing the positions from which they would fire with a sniper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did these snipers --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To clarify the situation it would be good to indicate in the transcript. I believe that the witness had indicated on the photograph what he meant. He could point with a pointer where the fire was coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I didn't notice the witness pointing at something, but if, would you please then make clear that it appears in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, could you please put the pointer on the place that you say fire was coming from.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates] From above this black line. This is the area that the snipers were active from mostly you can see it here or around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the record, the witness indicated a circle around what appears to be the top five storeys of the building above a dark-coloured line drawn through the approximate centre of the building that we see in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the fire that you said you saw coming from the Holiday Inn, you saw it coming through windows or through doors or through apertures, or did they knock out the wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the windows and through the hole in the walls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these holes that you speak of, were these holes that were knocked out of the wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on how many floors did they knock these holes out of the wall? Is it the same five floors that you indicated to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was an approximation. We know it could not be more than five, based on what you just showed us. About how many floors did they knock holes out of the wall --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately from three to four floors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said generally, in general reference to these Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. buildings, that these buildings accommodated ABiH soldiers. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the lower floors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you become aware that the Holiday Inn accommodated soldiers from the lower floors? I take it that this is a situation that you could see from your lines, you can see the lower floors from your lines; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't see it. But we saw the units passing and also the stories of the people who left the Muslim part of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What units did you see passing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim units. Snipers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they passing, on vehicles or on foot or what means of transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there is a translation problem. The headphones. The headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... but -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I wanted to say, and this is in the interest of the Prosecution, so that they can follow. What I think I heard the witness say in his own language was not only that he had seen - and this is line 15 - snipers, but that he had seen sniper units. The witness used the adjectival form and not the nominal form. That is, he was referring to units as such, organisations that had been established on the Muslim side and I am not certain, but I think this is a very slight translation error. It hasn't been entered into the transcript. It only says "snipers" where it should say "sniper units." Obviously this is a question that could be raised but I am raising this for the sake of the Prosecution so that they can carry on with their procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, should we ask the witness to put his headphones back on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please put on your headphones again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we return to the last question, just to clarify something, is it your evidence that the holes knocked in the wall or the walls on the three to four storeys of the Holiday Inn had a radius of about 1 metres, the size of the holes was a radius of about 1 metre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't measure it. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am approximating. I am asking you to approximate. Or -- withdrawn. May I put it this way, in respect to the size of the holes, did you say, these holes were about a size of or a radius of 1 metre? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, more or less. It is something like that. It depends on which one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the biggest one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the size of the biggest one, approximate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a minute ago, about 1 metre. But I don't know. I didn't measure it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. You said you saw Muslim sniper units passing by. How, by what means of transport did they pass? Did they walk? Did they ride horses? Did they travel in cars? Did they -- how did they travel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the Jewish cemetery, on foot. There were also vehicles, armoured units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to -- let's go back to where we started from. I asked you how is it you knew that the Holiday Inn accommodated ABiH personnel, and you said that you saw these units passing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that people were leaving Sarajevo and that there were snipers who fired from the Holiday Inn. People would arrive, they would be transported in armoured vehicles. What you could see by our side by the Holiday Inn, but over there, perhaps it wasn't visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see persons being transported by armoured vehicles in the vicinity of the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the field of vision is very restricted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. Could you see these Muslim sniper units on foot in the vicinity of the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but very few metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "very few metres" could you explain a little bit further what you mean? You could only see them for an -- or within an area of very few metres; that the what you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me clarify this. Between the Holiday Inn and the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. What number was the Assembly building, could you remind us, please? Number "1?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the Executive Council and the Assembly, numbers "1" and "2."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you could see these sniper units between these buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were curtains in this part. This part of the Assembly. There is only a bridge there, the Vrbanja Bridge, and there were huge curtains between the Slovenijales building which is the right side of the Assembly. So it wasn't possible to see them. But after you fired, you could see the firing from the holes and the windows of the Assembly and the Executive Council. That's not very far from where we were, as the crow flies. It is 250 metres, as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am trying to understand what you are saying. Did you say, I try to remember what you have been telling us, did you say in answer to my question "Could you see these Muslim snipers on foot of the vicinity of the Holiday Inn," did you respond: "Yes, but very few metres,"? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you said it, was it true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I was there. I spent four years there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, notwithstanding the difficulties of vision, it was possible from some of the areas where your battalion or your company was located to see persons on foot on the streets in the vicinity of the Assembly building and the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection. May I? How should I express myself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object because this question represents -- misrepresents the witness's testimony. This witness did not speak about the neighbouring area. He specifically pointed out on the monitor the area between the Holiday Inn and the Executive Council. And I don't think that that was added into the transcript. I think it should be. He said that the only place where one could see -- the only place one could see was between these two buildings, and nothing else. So, asking this question in a general sense and saying, could you see this in the surroundings of the Holiday Inn, this does not correspond to the testimony that the witness gave. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: My --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin, one of the questions put to the witness and asked by the witness was: "Did you see -- could you see these Muslim sniper units on foot in the vicinity of the Holiday Inn?" The answer was: "Yes, but a few metres." So the objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Mr. President, nevertheless, since the witness later on specified this, could we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp is allowed to ask questions even if the later answers might be slightly different and perhaps Mr. Stamp wants to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. know exactly what the answer is, if you put a question in a different way. He is allowed to do so. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but, Mr. President, my question was different. Could we see in the transcript what the witness mentioned. He said that -- encircled the area between the two buildings. Could this be entered into the transcript so that it is clear. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the Holiday Inn is numbered, number "3" and the other buildings are "1" and "2." So I don't think for the transcript it is a problem that it has not been described again, since it becomes clear enough from the marked photograph. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall when it was -- or before I leave that area, may I just ask you one question: These persons that you say you saw on foot that you describe as snipers, how did you know that they were snipers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had black clothes down by the Jewish cemetery, and when we captured them, when they were killed in our part of the territory, this is what we could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just have a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I just ask you, I am at least a bit confused. The earlier questions were about military people passing by in-- well, let's say the other side of the river. Whereas the answer of the witness seems to relate -- I don't know whether this is something you would like to clarify before you pass on to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may have a moment to confer, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I wish you to think specifically of the snipers that you say that you saw on foot in the vicinity of the Holiday Inn. How did you know that those snipers that you saw on foot in the vicinity of the Holiday Inn were snipers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Going from the positions on the way from the positions back home where my flat is about 700 metres from the Jewish cemetery, we had observers every day. We had observed where snipers were active in order to neutralise those snipers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that these -- that you knew there were snipers because you had observers or are you saying that you knew they were snipers because your flat is 700 metres from the Jewish cemetery? May I just repeat the question: Those snipers -- those persons that you say you saw on foot in the vicinity of the Jewish -- in the vicinity of the Holiday Inn, why do you say they were snipers, simply?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we had binoculars, so it was possible for us to see everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now where were these observation posts from where you could see and be certain about what you saw, located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from elevated points of Vraca, the Jewish cemetery, Grbavica, Pulica [phoen], Drveta [phoen], Kuce [phoen] it was possible for us to observe this from these elevated points. Everything that served as a shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you know the route from -- that one would take from Grbavica to Pale?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very well. I've been down that route 150 times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that route exposed to ABiH sniping from Colina Kapa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the only route which provided a link to Grbavica. It was one of the main roads. It was the only route to the outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That main road towards Pale went through Zlatiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was used by those who dared to use it, and people who didn't know about it. So they would use the road and then be killed by a sniper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that road, was there a coffee shop known as "Kod Stane?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that road, apart from Colina Kapa, where did sniping from the ABiH emanate from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from all directions. From Sarajevo, Debelo Brdo, Staro Brdo, Mojmilo, and from elevated points in the direction of the Sarajevo-Pale Road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You got sniping from Debelo Brdo, you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, where the French UNPROFOR Battalion was located, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You got sniping from some parts of Staro Brdo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Sarajevo Romanija Corps controlled some parts of Staro Brdo? One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you could assist, Mr. Usher, if you could take the photograph. I think it is distracting the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Question: The Sarajevo Romanija Corps controlled a part of Staro Brdo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will clarify this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just answer me. Did the Sarajevo Romanija Corps control a part of Staro Brdo and ABiH another part of that hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I would have to clarify this for the sake of the truth. When the UNPROFOR forces arrived, the Muslim forces dug in in Debelo Brdo. So they arrived at the rear of the Serbian Army. This has been recorded on tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, on that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, the question was about Staro Brdo, and your answer was, as it was translated, about Debelo Brdo. Was your answer about Debelo Brdo or about Staro Brdo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are linked to each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And along that route to Pale, did you come under fire from ABiH forces in Cicin Han?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On part of the road above Zlatiste.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you came --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you came under fire of ABiH forces at Cicin Han?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if the positions were a little closer to our positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You came, I take it then from your answer, that you came under fire from ABiH forces in the direction of Cicin Han, but a little bit closer to the road; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Muslim snipers would appear and do what they would do, and then they would withdraw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that road to Pale, did the Muslim snipers, as you call them, also fire from Brajkovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Brajkovac is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Brajkovac. Yes, I know. I know where Brajkovac is, not Rajkovac. I'm talking about the action towards our side, From Debelo Brdo, Staro Brdo and the Vraca-Spomenko road, and the Vraca and Grbavica, and Zlatiste parts, this is where snipers were most active. Children were killed, pregnant children, small children, a small child was killed by a sniper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I am trying --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My son was killed by a sniper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What we are trying --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter corrects himself. My son was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. shot at by a sniper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry to hear that. However, please try to understand what I am trying to do for the time being, is to identify where were the sources of this sniper fire from the ABiH on that road to Pale. Was there sniper fire on to the road from Brajkovac from ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there at the position all the time. You understand. I can say -- I can talk about the part where I was present on a daily basis, day and night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not say, Witness, that you travelled that route many times, that one had to be intrepid in order to take that route. I am asking you if you know of a danger of sniper fire from the ABiH emanating from Brajlovac [sic] when you look that route.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew about that because I would travel. My woman -- my wife and child were in Pale in 1992. I went to visit her and then I would return. This took about an hour, and then I would return.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to clarify things. In respect of the locations mentioned by Mr. Stamp, you said Brajlovac but I think you refer to Brajkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Brajkovac, yes. Forgive my pronunciation. Brajkovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you personally experience sniper fire coming from Brajkovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. They hit an old military lorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 12 or 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, this was in your presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was also present when the Muslims launched an attack --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am just asking whether you were present when this happened. Did you experience at more occasions sniper fire coming from Brajkovac? Was it once or was it more times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Mr. Stamp asks you about the direction --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From Brajkovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Mr. Stamp asks you about sniper fire, would you please, if he asks you to do so, tell him whether you personally experienced sniper fire. If he wants more details, he will ask for it, or that you heard about sniper fired from the locations you mentioned. If he needs more details, he will ask you. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just indicated to me that this may be an important time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't want to stop you, where I interrupted you already. We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the break we were talking about the road that you travelled on on countless occasions during the conflict, and the danger of sniping which you endured as you travelled on that road. The sniping, generally speaking, in the area that we spoke about, came from the north of that road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not a very precise question. We should give a precise location. It could be just one little slip and all the cardinal points would be modified. It could just be a curve in the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will hear that from the witness. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area that we talked about earlier, Debelo Brdo, Brajkovac, Cicin Han, the sniping that you referred to came from the north of the road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in relation to our positions which is towards the west.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the sniping come from the north of that road in those areas that we spoke of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly it was the eastern side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could the witness, with your leave, Mr. President, be shown, I think it is Exhibit D1778.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I have a look at that map. Thank you. That is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please point to the road on that map?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could the map be centred. Some of what he is pointing to is not...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From Vraca, then it goes to Miljevci and then on to Pale via Trebevic. Zlatiste and Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has pointed to a road outlined in yellow starting from a yellow area in which it is written "Spomen park Vraca" going easterly or towards the east just below where it is written "Vranjace" and continuing above where it is written "Zlatiste" and continuing to below where it is written "Stari Grad."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am correcting -- it is not Vranjace, it's Vranjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Vranjaca, thank you very much. That map could be removed, with your leave, Mr. President. And could he be shown 1779.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see a circle close to the middle of the map below the number "58"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that circle touch upon and include the same road that you pointed to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but only a very small part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said at all times the area covered by that circle was under the control of the ABiH. May I ask you this: On the countless occasions when you travelled this road, was that road under the control of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The road was on a neutral part. On this side was the Muslim Army and on this side was the Serb Army. That's why the road was exposed to sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point to the side where you say the Serbian Army was, exactly where it was in the vicinity of that circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pardon me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates] The Serb Army. [Indicates] BH Army, below the road itself, BH Army. It is on a slope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you travelled on that road which you have just described as neutral territory, did you see ABiH vehicles or ABiH troops travelling on that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not by the road. We used the road. Because from our positions --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your army, it is your evidence, used that road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Occasionally, when we thought the sniper wouldn't fire and that shells wouldn't be thrown on it, we used otherwise the roundabout road to Pale via Kasindol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we would use it at our own risk. It is a very long way to go via Kasindol and whoever dared who would use this road via Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. Can I take it from what you have been saying that at least some of the area covered by this circle was under the control of your army, the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. On -- could you please take your earphones off. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. On what basis, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? Use abstract terms if possible.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. Thank you. The witness used a very precise expression which was a perfect antonym of the question that was used. And I think I was abstract enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you were abstract enough. But in cross-examination the same might not be true in examination-in-chief. But in cross-examination the Prosecutor is allowed to ask this question. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question simply is -- oh, sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we understand from your evidence that at least some of the area covered by that circle on this map was under the control of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of my testimony, you can't understand this, if I said something else. It was a neutral area. If you have misunderstood me I will explain again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark on that map where you say the VRS lines were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions, I already tried to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May he be given a blue pen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With a dotted line or a full line?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With a dotted line or a full line, whichever one you prefer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's not in here --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to see where the lines were in that position. Could you now have another look at Exhibit 1778. And keep that one. Keep that one. You can look at both of them at the same time. Would you agree with me, Witness, that the positions that you marked for the VRS lines, north of Zlatiste, are different on these two maps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps I didn't mark it in properly, but I can do it again. I did it just -- I did it just so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can perhaps mark it according to the street names. That would be the best, to correct what was there. The Jewish cemetery I have marked in correctly, for certain. The 4th Company goes along Ljubljanska Street and Zagrebacka Street towards Vrbanja. That's been put in correctly, 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP11, please listen to questions put to you. If Mr. Stamp wants to know additional information, he will ask you for it, please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you that on the map in front of you, 1779, that area of the circle, that road that you travelled on was under the control of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious that you weren't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is your answer? I suggest to you that in the vicinity --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Usher, you may take those maps now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Of the Jewish cemetery, the VRS controlled the chapel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VRS never, from the start of the war to the finish, never had under its control the chapel at the Jewish cemetery. Never, and I will state this before this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you, sir, that the area to the east -- sorry -- the area to the west of the Jewish cemetery was high ground which overlooked much of the city of Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not very high.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest that it overlooked much of the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but buildings, houses, hill Zuc, Hum, Sokolac, Mojmilo, Sogbunar, and then over there towards Bistrik, Bjelave, and further on, Metas, Kosevo Hospital, and so on, Kosevo stadium, it is a large area of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you agree with me notwithstanding that Hum on the other side was high areas and there were other areas. That area, on the western side of the Jewish cemetery overlooked much of the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends from which side you look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I further suggest to you that that area or from -- withdrawn. I suggest to you that from that area to the west of the Jewish cemetery, it was possible to fire infantry weapons into the city of Sarajevo. Was it possible or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You say it was possible, but we didn't fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I -- may I instruct you to answer to the questions and if you are asked for a possibility, then just tell counsel whether it was possible or not possible. If he wants to know whether you did it, he will ask for it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that you are able to tell us where the lines of the various companies of your battalion were located because you, at some time or the other, fought with all these companies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those that were closer to me, I can say for certain about them, on my right and my left-hand side, the 5th and the 4th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's take those two. When did you fight with the 5th Company? Yesterday I think you told us you could tell us the dates. Can you tell us when you fought with the 5th company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the occasion of the attack of the Muslim forces, the operation that was called --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Beginning. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I ask "when" I am asking that you tell me, the month, the year, the date, even the hour, if you can. When did your unit, your company, fight with the 5th Company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you straight away. On the 12th of June, 1992, in the early hours of the morning the attack started and it lasted incessantly until the dark fell, and it went on -- let me just finish since you asked and since I was the only one who survived this attack without a scratch, although the Muslims had even used poisonous gases, my military specialty was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP11, the question is when it was, not what means were used, but the question was when did you fight. And I do understand when you said that on the 12th of June in the early hours of the morning, the attack started, that you indicate that that was the beginning of the fighting. But listen to the questions and answer to the questions. Although, I am fully aware that you have far more information that you think would be useful for this Court to know, but nevertheless, since the Prosecution has not all time available to it, to listen to the questions and to answer. So I take it that you say that the fighting started on the 12th of June in the morning. It went on until when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the only time your unit, your company, was engaged in combat with the 5th Company or were there other times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were other times as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were engaged in combat with the 5th Company, who did you receive your orders from to join them in combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked for volunteers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive orders to join them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I said, they asked for volunteers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ever join you in the defence of your area of responsibility, that is, did the 5th Company ever join you in the defence of your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not they volunteered or they were ordered Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. It was a -- an intense attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am wrapping up, Mr. President. If I may just take a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The persons on foot that you described as snipers which you said you saw in the vicinity of the Holiday Inn, were they carrying sniper weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of weapons you would describe as sniper weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is hard to observe, but there were long-barreled weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what a Dragonov is?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise, but I am following the French channel, and I did not have the ending of the witness's answer. Could he please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in English it reads: "It is hard to observe, but there were long-barreled weapons." Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you see them -- I am sorry, how often did you see them carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise to interrupt you, but you asked me if I knew what Dragonov was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I presume that that is a sniper rifle, according to the French word.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand French?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I know it's a French word.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Have you ever seen one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would you see these snipers or persons that you thought were snipers in the vicinity of the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, occasionally, in the course of observation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you help us a little bit more with what you mean by "occasionally"? More than once a day? Once a week? Once a month? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we were observation posts, we had our observers in case there was an attack. We had observers who would submit reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how often? Just, if you could specify a little bit more what you mean by "occasionally."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had observers who were there every day. We wouldn't have managed to get through such a war with very few people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you see these people approximately every day; is that your answer? Or would they be seen approximately every day? The question is withdrawn. Would you personally see these persons that you thought were snipers approximately every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't. I didn't go to observe every day. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Quickly, you mentioned that you knew of two facilities where the ABiH Army manufactured weapons of war. When was the first time during the conflict this came to your knowledge and attention?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did you obtain -- well, before I ask that. Did this knowledge come to your attention in 1992 in respect to both facilities or only one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For Vaso Miskin Crni it was in 1992 when people came from Sarajevo to our territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did the other facility that you mentioned being a weapons producing facility, when was this -- when did this become known to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also in 1993 and 1994. People who came to our positions would speak about it. People who came -- men who came to bring our unit up to strength.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard about the one in Vaso Miskin in 1992 and the first time in respect to the other would be 1993; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, more or less, yes. I can't remember the exact dates. Many things have happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear these men who came to your side speak about these things personally? Did you personally hear them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that information and knowledge have come to the attention of your superior officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including your artillery officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we reported on what we found out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am -- would, Mr. President, would like to ask a question. Perhaps I can ask it and it could be ruled as to whether or not the question is a proper question. I was going to put it to the Court, first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would it do any harm if the witness would hear the question or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, Mr. DP11, not to answer the question until permission has been given for it. For the next question. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have had evidence in this court from an artillery officer in respect to the artillery targets in the vicinity of Grbavica and the Jewish cemetery. He never mentioned any of those two locations. Do you have an explanations to why these two locations would not be targets for your artillery if it was well known in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, on what basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection. Because the person we are speaking about indicated that he had left that place in 1993, and it seems that one of the targets that we are speaking about was brought to the knowledge of the units in 1996. So there is some chronological confusion created by the Prosecution. I think the Prosecution should clarify this immediately. And it was brought to the attention in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President -- I apologise. This witness left the scene in 1992, not 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber deems this question and the answer to this question not to be of assistance for the determinations the Chamber has to make. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I will move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
