utterances.text: Could I answer?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just be sure that -- I see on my transcript, you asked to answer that question. But the Chamber -- the Chamber has not allowed this question to be put to you so there is no need to answer the question. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you were given orders or your units were given orders not to fire on civilians; is that so? As a matter of fact, the person who asked you the question told you that you were ordered not to fire on civilians, and you answered "yes." Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you further said and I quote: "Yes, I could explain this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. better. We received orders every three days or every five days." Is that corrects to the frequency in which you received these orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depended on the need. As the first men arrived and as the unit was brought up to strength because the new men had to be provided with information with regards to the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in respect of the frequency, it was approximately every three to five days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said then as you are saying now, that it depended on the need, on what was required at the time, and I think you started to explain. Could you explain what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I just said that new men arrived, the unit would be brought up to strength because there were wounded and dead men all the time, and this depended on what was required. I can't say whether it was every three or five days or occasionally, all the time. But on the whole it was almost all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be necessary for your units to be ordered every three to five days not to fire upon civilians if you could not see civilians, and if your weapons could not hit the civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we couldn't see them and -- well, if we couldn't hit them, no, it wasn't necessary to receive orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is the end of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... as I understood. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is there any need to re-examine the witness? Or I should ask Ms. Pilipovic who started the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Willingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will. Thank you, Mr. President. Re-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, in response to a question put to you by the Prosecution, page 35, line 6 to 10, you said that the positions referred to by the Prosecution, that is to say the red circle, the positions of the Serbian Army under the red circle you saw on the map, you said that these positions were on the road. Do you remember your answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You also added with regard to the nature of the terrain, you said that the terrain was on a slope, I think. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, a slight slope towards the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, my question is as follows: As far as you know in the zone of the red circle was there ever a post of any kind on a permanent basis of VRS soldiers throughout the period that you were familiar with; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I am going to move on to the issue of the definition of "lines." When the Prosecution asked you a question about the line, the position of the line, you didn't draw a continuous line, and you said, do you want me to tell you what there is in the spaces in between. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Can I clarify this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 37.3. 37.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Of the French or the English transcript, may I ask of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have only on our screen the English transcript, so it could not be the French, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Defence counsel would be very happy to have the French transcript in front of it. I don't know if this is the time to say it. 37.3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember this, Witness? Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell this Trial Chamber what you meant when you said "the spaces between" the intervals in the line that you draw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was a neutral zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, Mr. Piletta-Zanin I would like to go back to one of your earlier questions. That is about page 35, line 6 to 10. You confronted the witness with this answer, that the ABiH Army was on the road, you said. Could you please indicate where I find this on these lines. Because it is the recollection of the Chamber that in French it was "sous la route" and that is in English, "below the road."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I was relying on what I heard in the witness's language and I was following him in his own language. I am closer to him. If the transcript was French, but that's not the case, it is in English. How it was reproduced, I really don't know. I think we have certain translation problems, perhaps more than usual, but this is what the witness said. I can find it. But at line 37.3, yet again it is one of his interventions, time consuming interventions, the line 37.3, and I will read this in the transcript which we don't have in the French yet, the witness was saying what is not here, what is missing. And at 37.3, I have it before me, I don't know how I could improve on this, how I could say it in any better manner. We are losing -- wasting time, unless we don't have the same numbers, the same figures or the same idea of justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just go back to where Mr. Stamp the last time objected, because I then asked for further information on page 36, line 6 to... Yes. That was about 37, line 3. Is that -- is that problem solved, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, it is not. And I think the best way we could go about it, I am not pressing the point, is if my learned colleague is going to refer to the evidence, he could just read what the evidence is, if he has it there. Because his paraphrasing is not precisely what was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Part of the guidance that will be given during the next few days to the parties would be how to refer to the other sources. Because this creates a problem again and again. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that I have just quoted very precisely. I have just quoted very precisely what the witness said at line 37.3. I have quoted it twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Put the question to the witness and use the words as precise as possible. Please proceed. I can't imagine that the witness has the question clearly in his mind any more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, exactly, Mr. President, that I want to say that this sort of objection is not acceptable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this is what you stated, "and if you want me to tell you what there is in between," and you were interrupted. Between the line that you were drawing. Could you tell us, please, what you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That our units, our trenches weren't there. It was a neutral zone. We didn't have enough men to cover all the territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you are telling us if I have understood you correctly, that your line was not a continuous one, but that there were certain empty zones in your line itself. Is that how we are to understand it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, in response to a question from the Prosecution, you also mentioned the Hum, Zuc, Sokolac, et cetera, points, and Mojmilo. Who was at those sites, could you remind us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me correct you. It is not Sokolac, it's Sokolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. Who was present at these sites?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH Army was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. From these sites could one observe, was the vision of the town direct; yes or no? Was it possible to see the town directly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for most of them. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a hypothesis, but one could fire at the town; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from one of these sites or from any of these sites, was -- were there any shots fired at the part of the town where you resided, that is to say, Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, in response to a question from the Prosecution, you said something that made me tremble. You mentioned the use of gas by one of the armies. Could you please tell us what you were referring to and what personal knowledge you have of this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The reference the witness made to the use of gas was not in response to the question I asked. It was not responsive. Neither is it really relevant to the issues before the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue was not -- did not arise from questions put to the witness in cross-examination, and apart from that, I would advise you also to refrain from any comments. What answers would make you tremble is a different matter. Please move to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But nevertheless, one should know. Because, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is important to know, then certainly the Defence will call witnesses who can give information on this subject. And perhaps they are calling witnesses. So I hope you do understand that not all of the information on the entire armed conflict can be heard from you. So I am not saying it is irrelevant. I am not saying that we will not hear about it, and I do understand that you feel it of importance for this Chamber to know. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order to make everything clear, may I ask a question about the fact that the Defence has just discovered; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You just discovered the issue you want to put to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Personally, yes. I will check this with Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have just discovered this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, you can put a question if it is a matter you just discovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that certain chemical weapons were used. What do you know personally about this? What can you tell this Trial Chamber about this, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Same objection, and I don't think he said chemical weapons, but gas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, some people refer to gas as being chemical substances, so that would not be something -- let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I did not say "gas." I said "poisonous gases."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you are supposed not to comment on questions put to you. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- Briefly add a question, since one of the bases for counsel introducing this new area is that it is just learned to the Defence, just learned by the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was the basis of -- could I ask you to take off your headphones, Mr. DP11.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just inquire of the Defence through the Court, of course, whether or not some of the documents they have submitted to us, served to us, made reference to this use of poisonous gases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the question is whether the material disclosed to the Prosecution contains any information about the use of poisonous gases?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is a very good question and I have to admit I have to be cautious. It is impossible for me to know whether in all the documents that were provided there was -- mention was made of such arms, such poisonous gases were mentioned even if it was in an indirect manner. I can't answer that question, but we are discovering about this through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I see well that your client might want to confer with you? Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Galic has just indicated that probably in the military documents, there are documents that are mentioning in a general way the problem of weapons, that is, of poisonous gases. But as far as we know, we do not have any documents of the use of combat gases in relation to this testimony. So this is something that I discover now. I believe that it is the duty of each and everyone to hear what this witness has to say and not to object to what he has to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you intend to call witnesses on the issue? I mean, is there in any of the summaries of the witnesses any reference to the use of these gases?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that is an enormous problem now because the Prosecution has told us about a campaign. Now, if we discover that the other side may have used no matter to what extent, perhaps a little, perhaps a lot, weapons that are strictly forbidden by all the conventions that we know, we find ourselves in a very different dimension of the conflict. I don't know how I am going to act in the future. As far as we are concerned, I have to say it again, for us, this is a completely new fact. Now, if he is talking about poisonous gas, this is literally combat gas, then maybe we can find out about it a little later and find out more clearly what it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if in the material disclosed to the other parties, the use of poisonous gas is indicated, let me put it cautiously, it is -- one could expect that this would be an issue that would be put forward by the Defence. Until now, I didn't hear anything about it. But, well, we don't know how the Defence case will develop. And even if I am not aware of any mention made to it, you may put some questions to the witness and we will, of course, we will have to assume that it is entirely new in this specific context that you learned about it today. So, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in order whatever -- could you please put on your headphones. Now, Witness, I am going to start again. You tell us, tell this Chamber, what you know in relation to what you yourself defined as being use of combat gas, this is how it would be translated into French, that is, poisonous substances. What do you know about the use of these substances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in order to prove that the Muslim army was armed with all kinds of weapons, they had a nitroglycerin rifle. They used gases. They used gases. Every army knows what that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I am going to stop you. Witness, you said they were using gases. Are these gases that were launched towards the army, towards the troops, there are historic examples and I don't wish to quote here, were these gases that were designed here to destroy personnel and urban areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Killing of troops and anything else that was in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know whether in the English transcript, in the English transcript we have the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. same thing in French. I see that we are speaking about the yperite gas. I don't see that -- we see it in the English transcript. I believe that is the yperite, which is the mustard gas and I am not sure if this is the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this again this is all translated to the witness. If there is any -- if there is any need to be clarified, it is not to interpret the answers of the witness at this very moment in his presence and his headphones on. Let me just --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Mr. President, what I am saying is what I heard in the French transcript which doesn't appear in the English transcript. I believe this is my duty --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, there is no problem to say that there is a difference in the English and the French transcript. Then you ask the witness to take his earphones off. Then you tell us what you heard in French and then we read or we remember what we heard in English. But to make comparisons and to see whether this is a certain kind of gas is not the thing you do in the presence of the witness. Yes. But let me first -- because -- let me just ask a few questions to see whether there is any basis for continuing. You talked about the use of gas. When did you hear about it, did you experience it yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in 1992, on the 12th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the 12th of June, you experienced it yourself. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please proceed and specifically ask questions about the personal experience of the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, since you had personal experience of this, did you know people who were affected by this use of this harmful substance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke of an attack where you were the only one who survived. Can you tell us if this was this attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that very attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The people who didn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... improperly leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please refrain from leading, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. And please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, why, if you know, did the soldiers die, those who were with you, during this attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were hit by glycerin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean -- no further question. Thank you. Very last thing. You spoke about defections going across the line, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were these defections of soldiers, of civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everybody fled and no matter which faith they had, which religion they were of.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions to you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I would like Exhibit 1781 to be put on the ELMO. I am sorry. Exhibit 1781, yes. That is not the one. 1781. I have this one. Is this?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 1781?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: This one? That one. You said that the chapel was within the red circle. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the very corner of the cemetery on the Muslim side. I said it properly, and our position goes from here, not directly from the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Are you able to put a dot or something in exactly the place, but use a different colour, a red one, for example.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Did you say that the BH Army controlled the chapel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: One of the witnesses that we -- that came here in one of these days said the following, answering the question. The question was: "This building that you call chapel, which force occupied it, if any?" The answer was: "No one held it. It was closer to our positions." And I think that "our positions" was in this case the VRS positions. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: My last question is: Who did control the cemetery itself? Because as far as I understand you were on the west side and the BH Army on the east side. But the cemetery itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neutral.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Neutral. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Nieto-Navia also has one question to you -- Judge El Mahdi, I apologise. JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Sir, you said that each company had a sniper, one sniper; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Through the establishment structure. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. Well, your one, the one that was attached to your company on the front line, he carried out his duties, his task of sniping from the lines that you held or was he in a protected position, a more elevated position? Could you perhaps elaborate on this, according to what you know, to your personal experience? Where was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. He was directly on the line every day if he was there, if he was not absent, and his task was to neutralise the enemy that was advancing on us. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So, at a distance, if I understand correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At a distance, distance between us was 30 to 50 metres. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. You also said that you were able to establish the existence of snipers on the other side. Could you please look at me, Witness? Sir? Could you please look at me? Could you please look me in the eye so that I can communicate to you, rather than you look to your right or to your left? Very well. So, you are saying that you were able to establish the existence of units of sniper units on the other side, that is on the side of the Presidency, that they were walking in the streets going to or coming from their positions, either their positions in Holiday Inn or in the neighbouring buildings. Now, you were able to establish this yourself from your positions or was it that your observers were telling you, they told you this information, were these units visible where passers-by visible in the street from your positions that were to the west of the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained this once and I will explain it again. Only one small part of the street when we were going to reconnaissance because I was the commanding officer of the platoon, I went at a certain period if there was no younger person to do it, I had to go. If there was no junior to do it, I had to go. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] As an observer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And the protection, if I understand correctly, there were these protections that the other side had erected in order to hide the view from your positions, was that effective protection or were you still able to see, to observe, the persons passing by, among others, the sniper units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The screen was effective but it was possible to see it from the other side, as the observers, the reconnaissance people went from the other side, 1, 2 kilometers to other side to Vraca, and Vraca is a very high point. So there were buildings, there were trees. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] From your side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you. You indicated to us that you travelled from your positions to Pale some 150 times on that road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you travelled from your positions to Pale, would the higher part of the hill be on your right-hand side or your left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends on the terrain. On the right-hand side is a lot higher, but the left-hand side is also quite high in various areas of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us where it was higher -- where it was high as well on the left-hand side? What areas? I do not need every single spot, but where would you, in the beginning or could you please indicate where --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beginning, in the middle and just by the end of our area of responsibility, of the area of the responsibility of our battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we look at the Exhibit 1781 -- no. I am making a mistake. I am sorry. I invite you to look at Exhibit 1780. And could you please look at where the red circle is. Would the higher ground be below that circle or more in the direction of the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not quite sure exactly where this is, but towards the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it is the portion of the road I think you told us about -- I beg your pardon? I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The higher ground would be? Could you please indicate that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The higher ground would be from the road in the direction of the city rather than --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- In the direction of Zlatiste? So Zlatiste was lower than --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am asking you, on that spot whether since that road is on a hill, on a slope of a hill, as far as I understand, whether the lower part of the hill was to the north, that is, on the map above, or whether the lower part of the hill was to the south, that is, lower on the map? Please indicate where was the lower part and where was the upper part of the hill.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, the terrain is such that there are rocks, there are elevations on both sides, on both sides of the road. So I don't know what the height is. I can't say it exactly. Because the terrain is mountainous, hilly, and there are rocks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In general, where the circle is, could you indicate where the higher part of the hill is and where the lower part of the hill is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly. I don't want to tell a lie. I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. You've told us that you did observe now and then, when the juniors were not able, the opposite positions. Could the witness please be shown map 1778, and could he be give an red pen. Would you tell us exactly from where you observed when juniors were not there and when you had to fulfill observation tasks, could you tell us from where exactly you then observed the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The memorial in Vraca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was that the only spot from where you observed or were there others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not the only one. It is not the only one. There were others as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you first put a small cross with the red pen on the monument from where you just told us that you observed the city.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please, with a red pen, put a small "O1" to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us from what other positions you observed the city, when you had to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We used different locations, trees. And then locations that were a little hidden so that we would shelter and then observe because it was risky business.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please indicate where, from where. So --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are no trees here. I can't indicate some parts that are not here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but from what area, apart from the one you indicated -- just indicated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of Vraca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that you were pointing with the pen to--

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire area of Vraca, for example, the upper side below the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The upper side below the road. You pointed at --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates] This, this here. This here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just -- for the transcript, could you please mark that area you just indicated with a red pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the observations were made from within that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ever observe from outside that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. You told us when answering a question from the Defence counsel that during the attack on the 12th of June that you were the only one who survived and the others were killed by glycerin. Could you explain to us what you mean by "glycerin"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that the others died from glycerin, but on the front line nobody survived in a sense that they were all either wounded or killed. But I also suffered from the affect of the tear gases, the blister gas, the tear gas. This was the combat --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you say the others where you were the only one who survived. The others were killed in what way and how many were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said there were wounded and killed, the others even Vojvode Slavko Aleksic who was the commander of the 5th Company, he was shot and wounded in the chest on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am asking -- you told us before that you were the only one survived. I do now understand that there were some people killed and that there were some people wounded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many were killed during this attack or as you called it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Approximately were these five, or 25 or 250?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 8 and the others were slightly wounded and those were wounded were taken to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then you told us that glycerin was used. You are talking about nitroglycerin rifles. What would you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a poison which destroys the human organism. It is a rifle with six cartridges. It is a short-barreled rifle. One of the soldiers had been killed in our area and we found it while we were doing the mopping up operation of the terrain the following day. And the other Muslim forces were taken out by the UNPROFOR later on when they came to those positions three months later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say one of those killed you found them when mopping up the area being hit by such a cartridge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't hit. He wasn't hit then, he was hit by our bullet. He had a rifle, a glycerin rifle on him, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you see anyone hit by such a cartridge, apart from having found such a rifle in the hands of the other party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it personally, but I felt the poison gases on that day. As I said, the blister gas or mustard gas, the tear gas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you are now mentioning three gases. They were all used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How do you -- how do you know that exactly? On what basis do you take it that these three gases, as you mentioned them, were used? Is this the same gas or are these three different types of gases?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were probably three different kinds. And I personally felt it on myself, on my own skin on the 12th of June. Because they couldn't break through at the end, they used that because I thought I was going to die. Before I never felt such a thing, I only learned about it a little bit, but only a little bit. I felt that I was falling apart. That's what I felt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What did you exactly feel -- no, let me just put a different question to you first. How did this gas come so close to you? Was it fired? Was it thrown? Was it -- in what way was it -- how did it reach the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably fired from a weapon because I was sprayed with blister gas. I didn't know it was blister gas, but I felt terrible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just first -- I will just go step by step. You say it was probably fired by a weapon. Why do you think it was fired by a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it landed right next to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It landed right next to you. And did then something explode or what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was intense. It was very noisy from the shells, so I couldn't hear everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you don't know whether anything exploded next to you or -- and then what did you feel, then, exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I started to suffocate. I felt I was falling apart, that my body was falling apart and I had felt itching on the parts of the body that were exposed, that means, my hands, my face and my lungs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was itching and it was -- what did you feel exactly as far as breathing was concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was dying from all the coughing. It was worse than being hit by a shell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What did you then do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remembered that moment to put a bandage on my mouth and my nose, and to put water on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you move away from the area where you were hit or what...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. I stayed there because the attack was ongoing, I was just firing at random. I was just firing in a burst. I never used single-shot fire because near the positions I was never in a position -- in a situation to use single-shot firing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you stayed in your position; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you seek help, medical help for your...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed until the end that day during the combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was for how many more hours? Because we do not know exactly at what time it happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe half an hour. An hour. I don't know. I didn't time it. Time passed by slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You told us about three kinds of gases. Could you tell us about what you experienced in respect of the other gases? Was it also your personal experience or did you hear about it or...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've mentioned the blister gas and the tear gas. I said that I felt this -- its effects personally. But others, they were hit by shots from a glycerin gun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, about the gases. Is it your testimony that these three gases were in this one projectile that landed near to you or were these different projectiles that contained these different gases?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each one was fired separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and where did the others fall? Next to you or near to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first two, near to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Near to you. Was that prior to the projectile you just described or was it afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember everything exactly. There was shelling for 12 hours, continuous shelling and shooting. They would fire from rifles and machine-guns and what have you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know whether it was prior or after the shell you just described. Could I ask you, what did you feel different -- did you have different experiences in respect of these other shells which, if I do understand you well, contained other gases or was it approximately the same?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned the blister gas and the tear gas. That's what I experienced. I didn't say that I had experienced the effects of glycerin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but the -- the events you just described where you felt that it was itching and where you put something on your mouth used water, was that blister gas or tear gas or mustard gas or how would you call that gas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said blister gas and tear gas. I mentioned both those gases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, was that in this one explosion that both gases were affecting you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not after the same one. I don't know how many explosions there were. I don't know if there were five explosions. But I experienced the effects of two separate explosions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and what was the difference between the one explosion and the other, in what you experienced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly about the explosion. I said that we were being shelled from all the directions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you. You told us exactly what you felt after the projectile landed you told us about before, feeling the itch, it did itch. Was that different from the other projectile?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the second time I started suffocating. My organism, my internal organs were falling apart. My head was splitting. I held on to the trigger and I fired, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and on the other occasion of the other projectile, you still don't know what was the first one and what was the second one? Because it is not quite clear to me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said about the -- I mentioned blister gas and this all took place within a few minutes, within a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, how did you decide it was blister gas? I mean, what do you know about gases?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I learned something about it while I was in the army, while I was in the JNA, the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you get medical help afterwards to recover from the effects of these gases?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after I left the position when the units arrived to help, I went to the first house. And there was a clinic in the vicinity, in Vraca, in Miljevci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was this a medical facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a small part, a small amount of medical supplies for first aid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they send you to a hospital, and to what hospital, if so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't want to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't want to go to a hospital. We will adjourn until 5 minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, may I ask the specific attention of the parties. If for the testimonies by videolink, if any exhibits are needed they should be provided not later than next Thursday to the Registrar. Is that clear? I see nodding. Everyone is nodding. For the transcript, all the parties are nodding. Yes. I have a few more questions for you, Mr. DP11. Did you report to your superiors the experience you described before the break, that is, that you suffered from gases?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the company commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know whether anything -- whether it went any higher up or do you know what consequences were drawn from your experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then my next question is: Did you observe on the other side of the lines, so that is in the BiH forces, did you ever anyone to use gas masks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because of the smoke screen creating by the shells, and it was very difficult to see anything. All you could hear were the explosions, the shells.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you ever observe at all during the conflict, the other party using gas masks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you told us during your examination that you observed to see sniping coming from the other side of the confrontation line, and that you needed these observations in order to neutralise them. How would you neutralise or how did you neutralise snipers at the other side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was necessary, the artillery would be used, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any -- so it was not -- was it your unit or was it another unit that would use artillery to neutralise snipers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the unit I said we had a number of mortars and anti-aircraft machine-guns, Pam, 12, 7, 12.7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would use these mortars to neutralise, if necessary, the snipers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If our line was close to the Muslim line, we would use 60 millimetre mortars, and we would use snipers against snipers, heavy artillery, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would use heavy artillery to neutralise snipers on the other side of the line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give me an example? Is there any specific event in your recollection where you use heavy artillery against sniper units or snipers? Do you remember what locations or you targeted with the heavy artillery when you wanted to neutralise these snipers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When killings occurred at the crossroads, when Miro Triskovic, who was pregnant and had been married for 11 years, another four men of ours died. We tried to get them out. On that occasion, we had to use heavy artillery in 1994, on the 6th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember where the sniper fire came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From where did it come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you neutralised it by using heavy artillery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a 40-millimetre gun, a Bofors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember exactly where the victim of the sniping incident you just mentioned was hit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I mean on what location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below the Bosut barracks at the cross-roads towards Sogbunar and Ohrid Street, in fact Trebevicka Street below Debelo Brdo, about 50 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say she was hit from a distance of 50 metres; is that correct or...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you used artillery from where exactly then? What distance would it be to the sniper nest from where the artillery unit was stationed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. 2 or 3 kilometres. I didn't measure it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for these answers. These were all my questions. I always hesitate to say that this concludes the evidence of the witness. You are standing, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I just want to check something in the transcript, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Could the witness take his headphones off, please. I will be very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to read out everything. In the English transcript that I am looking at, that what I would like to say is that the French transcript specifies that this victim was a young woman who was pregnant. This person that we are speaking of now who was allegedly hit by sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I didn't see it in that case. The question that I wanted to put, Mr. President regarded one of the questions that you put to the witness concerning the restriction of snipers by artillery, and if we are allowed to do so, I would like to be able to show the document that we had, the photograph that depicts the town of Sarajevo. With the Executive Council tower in it, et cetera. It is somehow here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What would you like to ask the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, willingly. Sir, my question is: On this photograph, there is a building which was seriously damaged. We can see artillery impact, the traces of artillery impact. And given the state of the building, given the extent of the damage inflicted on the building, I would like to know whether this relates to artillery fire which was necessary in order to eliminate sniper positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will allow you to put this question to the witness, but then I would have one additional question before doing so. Could perhaps the -- yes. You just told us about the neutralizing of sniper nests, and you gave us one example. Could you indicate precisely where that sniper nest was and perhaps a bit more precise because I might not have understood you perfectly well, when you answered that question. Where was that sniper nest that you neutralized, the sniper nest that from where fire came that hit, as the English transcript reads "a pregnant woman who had been married for 11 years." Where was that sniper nest exactly? Was it in a building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It was near the area of responsibility of the French Battalion of UNPROFOR, very near them, about 20 metres from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but where exactly, what street, what building, what side of the Miljacka river or -- it is not quite clear to me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't in a street. It was on Debelo Brdo because I said before in my testimony that the Muslims during the truce, when the French Battalion UNPROFOR arrived, they dug through a hill - just a moment - they dug a tunnel through the rock and they have put the snipers there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it was -- could you please -- could the witness be provided with the map number 1778. And could you mark with a red pen and a cross where the sniper unit was located that you neutralised.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is approximately here. About here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please put an "S" next to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: An "S"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, an "S." And could you also locate are the victim actually was when she was hit by this sniper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please put a "V" next to that red cross.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only have one question. Could we have on the ELMO the photograph in question with the assistance of the usher, please. This is this photograph where we can see the Holiday Inn and all the buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you. Further re-examination by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have shown us the tower, the Executive Council, which I believe bears the number "1;" is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, we see on this photograph the building -- the structure and the front that was damaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These damages, what are they linked to, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of combat operations. Because of the bullets, the inflammable bullets. Because of the shells that were fired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Why were these shots fired, do you think?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That question, as phrased, is really an invitation for the witness to speculate about the motives of a variety of people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just let me --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know if there is -- do you know a reason, if there is one, why was fire opened on this building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of sniper nests.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it pleases you, Mr. President. In respect to questions asked about the relative heights of the positions to the north or south of the circle on Exhibit 1780, I would ask that the witness be shown that exhibit again and if I may ask just a couple of questions about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. Further cross-examination by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see a horizontal -- a vertical line on that map which is intersected by a number "93"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean this line?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you refer to the colours, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a blue line going from top to bottom of the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the bottom of that line do you see the number "1080"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it abuts on to a circle, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be called that, yes. You mean this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, is that circle a contour line -- well, first, do you know what a contour line is on a map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hill?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You are saying that that is a hill. Now, I am asking, do you know what a contour line is on a map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an elevation point, it's an altitude point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see other contour lines going away from that hill in the direction of the circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the north of the circle, do you see other contour lines getting wider going towards where you see Cicin Han and the word "cemetery" on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the cemetery. There; not over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the word "Cicin Han"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here. I can see it here, Cicin Han, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see widening contour lines between the circle and the word "Cicin Han"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that indicate to you that from the circle to the direction of Cicin Han, the terrain was generally sloping downwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP11 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP11, this concludes your evidence in this court. I would like to thank you very much that you came and testified in this court. I know it is quite a distance. I thank you for giving answers to questions both -- of both parties and questions from the Bench. And I hope that you have a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank the Chamber, the Prosecution and the Defence, to the General, who listened to my testimony. I am glad that at least a part of the truth can be heard of what happened. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could we please be guided by you through the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D341, photograph, marked by witness; D331, photograph, entrance to the Jewish cemetery; D1777, pseudonym sheet, under seal; D1778, D1779, D1780, D1781, maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All these documents are admitted. D1777, under seal. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In respect of the next witness, the Chamber gives an oral decision as to the protective measures that is granted as requested. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, perhaps I will repeat in closed session what the name of that witness is so there should be no confusion. Please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, anything else?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We can call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please call the next witness. And I take it that pseudonym and facial distortion are effective. Pseudonym would be DP12? Ms. Pilipovic, it would be?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DP7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: DP7. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only thing I wanted to say, Mr. President, is that we will need a few minutes at the end of the session regarding translation problems, and I wouldn't want this to go over time. So could we please bear that in mind. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, two minutes will do. Two minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. DP7, because that's how I will call you, can you understand me -- can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving testimony--

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- The Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration they you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that declaration, which the text will be handed out to you now by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated. Your testimony will take only a few minutes today, and we will continue tomorrow. But then at least you have already experienced how the courtroom looks like. So it will only be have for a very short time today and then we will continue tomorrow. Ms. Pilipovic, should we turn into -- perhaps first if we would take the pseudonym sheet --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I will submit the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, I inform you that protective measures have been granted in respect of you, that means that your face will not be visible for the outside world and your name will not be used.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, first of all, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have a document before you where there is some information, your name, surname, date of birth, your father’s name. Is that correct, the information written on the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, are we in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No we are not. We turn into closed session. [Closed session].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that in 1992 you worked at the Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, you said something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you tell us throughout 1992, did you work all that year in the Kosevo Hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7
utterances.text: I worked until April that year. I don't exactly know which date it was, which day it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you worked until April, can you be precise? Was it the first half of April, from the first half of April or was it the second half of April, or the beginning of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7
utterances.text: It was until mid-April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you worked until mid-April, can you tell us, did you leave your work or was there another reason why you no longer went to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7
utterances.text: My first duty was 25 hours long because it is that kind of system that I worked -- operated on. And during that last duty that I had, there were some things that occurred which seemed very strange to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that after that duty you no longer went to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be a little more precise, when you say "some strange things." These strange things, were they the reason why you stopped going to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP7
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe this is a good moment to stop, considering there is a few minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. DP7, as I told you it will be only very short, but at least you made a start by now. We will continue tomorrow morning at 9.00 in the same courtroom. You are supposed not to speak with anyone about the testimony you give in this court. We will deal for two more minutes with procedural matters, and I will ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom and I hope to see you tomorrow morning. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you needed two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. It could be even shorter than that, but I am just waiting for the witness. Yes, thank you. Yesterday, we didn't have time to say it, but we have to say it, and I will do it very briefly, bearing in mind yesterday's pagination, in page 6, what is not in the transcript is the military specialty, I am talking about the French transcript, in 18:21, I believe that "inverted" could not have been interpreted as "bent" then a "fuse" should not be a "cord." In page 9, we have something which in the English transcript is a "quarry" and it could not be interpreted as a "department" in French, but more than anything, there are two points that I want to raise. It is just that it seems to us that in both of the transcripts we don't have the same thing, on page 59, in a sense that the witness who was speaking at the time, he was speaking about the tanks that were firing from the Hum hill, and this did not appear clearly in the transcript. There was one thing that seems to be important to underscore is that we are often -- we often hear things said about the Pam and Pat, P-A-M and P-A-T. Once we will be able -- we will have to have precise meanings of this. It was the Serbian booth that clarified this on one occasion, but it would be good to know what we are talking about. As far as the -- today's interpretation is concerned, I am afraid that what I said this morning when I came in was not translated. I was speaking about "genois," I was speaking about forewind, backwind and so on. I was speaking about "urnes" and all the other things, does not appear in the transcript. And neither does it appear now. So I suggest on one occasion we can just base ourselves on the French transcript and then just to translate it. That would be a lot easier. I have never spoken of a formal aspect, I have only spoken about nominal form which is a completely different thing. But as much as it is possible, we would like to have a proper translation of what I am saying. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that the interpreters do the utmost best to properly translate what whoever says in this court, and it is inevitable that sometimes mistakes are made. That's what happens and we will not change that, and I am confident that whatever observations you make in this respect will be taken very seriously, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, and it might be necessary to continue doing this. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Two matters very quickly, Mr. President. In relation to what my friend just said about Hum, it seems to be a complaint about the French and English transcript, and seems to be directed to the sense of meaning. I would not like there to be a change to the transcript without the Prosecution having the opportunity to consider it and respond. Secondly, since the beginning of the Defence case, the laptop used by the Prosecution lawyers in court has not been capable of doing a full text query search which causes us endless problems. We understand that in the near future, the laptop will be replaced by a new one. I wonder if something could be done in the meantime, because it does cause us problems when we can't search the transcript beyond a particular day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that surprises me. That might mean that the -- not all the transcripts are loaded in the computer. That might be the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, it is not, Mr. President. The button that one presses to activate the full text query --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just, if it would be allowed, and if you would press on the top the word "search" click on it, and then if you would then take in the third category full text query --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And that is not in black indicating that it cannot be accessed. We raised it with the technicians. I think I understand what the problem is. I think the only solution is a different machine, perhaps while we wait for a new machine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What surprises me, it is the machine, it seems to be a matter of the programme than of the machine because the machine hardly ever decides by itself whether something lightens up or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1.50 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 6th day of November, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
